purpose: Production integration candidate performance comparison; prior preview measurements were excluded.

method.comparison: Organic Flow disabled via test-only response shim vs enabled; Selected Ink Field and TRUNK remained active in both arms.
method.deterministicMode: Biography uses Manual A / Organic Contour; Artist Statement uses Hybrid Random with fixed 40/25/15/20 contributions. Only the test response and query are altered; repository source and production randomness remain unchanged.
method.metrics: Global requestAnimationFrame interval samples; Organic Flow engine snapshot draw timing, frame count, RAF active state, canvas/resolution/DPR/quality, Long Task API, and Chromium heap when available.
limitations: Headless Chromium results do not replace foreground physical-device acceptance.
Organic Flow OFF retains its loaded controller/resize observer while disabling its canvas and RAF, so this estimates incremental render cost rather than an unloaded page.
Performance classification is INCONCLUSIVE: observed RAF rates were unexpectedly low even in Organic Flow OFF, the browser ran headless, and hardware GPU telemetry was unavailable.

assessment.reason: The browser was headless and hardware GPU telemetry was unavailable. The Organic Flow OFF baseline itself showed severe and inconsistent frame delays, so the observed low FPS cannot be attributed to the candidate. Foreground hardware-accelerated acceptance remains pending.

observedAcrossTrials.longTaskApi: available; both arms reported frequent tasks

interpretation: Organic Flow ON added exactly one Organic Flow canvas per measured run; OFF removed that canvas and stopped its RAF.
Organic Flow drawing time stayed below the observed global frame delays, but the OFF baseline was also severely slow.
The repeated 10,000,000-byte heap value did not provide a usable memory trend.
No source or production random behavior was changed for the test; the response shim fixed the measured variant and mix only.
assessment.nextAcceptanceGate: Repeat the same conditions in a foreground hardware-accelerated browser before deciding production performance acceptance.
